html:
Compas, or konpa, is the dance music of Haiti, created in Port-au-Prince in 1955 by the saxophonist Nemours Jean-Baptiste. It is a smooth, steady style with guitars, horns and a strong beat.

It grew from the Dominican merengue and older Haitian rhythms, and soon became the favourite music of dance halls in Haiti. In the 1960s and 1970s smaller bands with electric guitars carried it to the diaspora in New York and Montreal.

Compas spread through the French Caribbean and Africa, and it was one of the roots of zouk in Guadeloupe and Martinique. It remains the sound of Haitian parties and of the yearly Carnival.
sum: Compas, or konpa, is the dance music of Haiti, created in Port-au-Prince in 1955 by the saxophonist Nemours Jean-Baptiste. It is a smooth, steady style with guitars, horns and a strong beat.
